answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public history of completed tasks; rewards route only to ledgers above a minimum depth, and transferring or splitting a ledger resets it to zero. A clone starts as a fresh vertex with no depth, so it earns nothing until it independently completes the same onboarding workload. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times that full workload, while honest agents pay it once. Like a sonnet's fixed form, the rule is rigid but cheap to follow honestly. The ocean of fake accounts gains no shortcut.
